 Top News Headlines In Indonesia, Laos, Myanmar, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand & Vietnam: Nov 20, 2026
 20/11/2026 09:11 AM 
 Labuan Bajo, Indonesia 
 INDONESIA  
 1.INDONESIA PARLIAMENT PASSES LONG-AWAITED ASSET FORFEITURE BILL -- ANTARA
 Indonesia’s House of Representatives (DPR) on Thursday passed the long-awaited Bill on Asset Forfeiture Related to Corruption and Other Crimes into law, concluding an 18-year legislative deliberation process.
 2.PRABOWO TO SUBMIT VICE PRESIDENTIAL NOMINEES ON NOV. 25: LAWMAKER -- ANTARA
 Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto will submit the names of two vice presidential candidates to the People's Consultative Assembly (MPR) on Nov. 25 ahead of next month's legislative vote to fill the vacant post, a senior lawmaker confirmed Thursday.
 LAOS  
 1.LAOS STUDIES 1,275-MW WIND POWER PROJECT -- VIENTIANE TIMES
 Laos has signed a development agreement with two companies for a proposed 1,275-megawatt wind farm in Savannakhet, launching a two-year feasibility study for regional power supplies.
 2.PROTECTING HEALTHCARE AGAINST CLIMATE RISKS -- VIENTIANE TIMES
 The Health Ministry is preparing a US$14.7 million (RM61 million ) operational plan for 2027 to strengthen primary healthcare and protect health facilities in five provinces against climate change.
 MYANMAR 
 1.BAY OF BENGAL INITIATIVE TO ASSIST LANDLOCKED MEMBERS -- THE GLOBAL NEW LIGHT OF MYANMAR
 The Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation (BIMSTEC) pledged to assist landlocked member countries, Nepal and Bhutan, in their development efforts, disaster preparedness, prevention, relief and rescue operations.
 2.AYEYAWADY’S MODERN FARMING TO BOOST YIELDS -- THE GLOBAL NEW LIGHT OF MYANMAR
 Ayeyarwady Region will encourage farmers to replace broadcast seeding with modern cultivation methods to improve yields across its more than 1.9 million hectares of cultivated land.
 PHILIPPINES 
 1.MARCOS PUSHES AI ADOPTION, REGIONAL COOPERATION VS ILLEGAL FISHING AT APEC -- PHILIPPINE NEWS AGENCY
 President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. on Thursday called for wider adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) among small businesses and stronger regional cooperation against illegal fishing during the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders’ Meeting here.
 2.ASEAN DIGITAL PACT TO WIDEN MARKET ACCESS FOR PHILIPPINE BUSINESSES -- PHILIPPINE NEWS AGENCY
 The ASEAN Digital Economy Framework Agreement (DEFA) is expected to expand regional market access for Philippine businesses, particularly small enterprises, by harmonizing rules on digital transactions, an economist said.
 SINGAPORE 
 1. MORE SUPPORT FOR RETRENCHED WORKERS, LONGER TRAINING STINTS FOR FRESH GRADS BEING CONSIDERED: JASMIN LAU -- CNA
 From fresh graduates seeking their first jobs to retrenched workers looking for a way back, more employment support could be on the horizon. 
 2. AXS, VISA AND MASTERCARD PARTNER TO LET AI AGENTS PAY BILLS WITHOUT MULTIPLE APP LOGINS -- THE STRAITS TIME
 Consumers may soon be able to pay their telco, electricity and healthcare bills, as well as housing loan instalments and fines, by speaking or typing a prompt to an artificial intelligence agent to do so on their behalf.
 THAILAND 
 1. CHIANG MAI OPENS ELECTRIC TRAM-STYLE BUS SERVICE WITH 15 STOPS -- THE NATION
 Chiang Mai has launched the all-electric, rubber-tyred Chiang Mai Tram by Lannatique, linking 15 stops around the old city with single journeys priced at THB20.
 2. NEIGHBOURS UP ARSENIC FIGHT -- BANGKOK POST
 The government is stepping up cooperation with Myanmar to trace the source of arsenic contamination in the Kok and Sai rivers in Chiang Rai, while accelerating efforts to provide safe alternative water supplies to affected communities.
 VIETNAM 
 1.HAI PHONG EYES MORE CHINESE INVESTMENT --  VIETNAMPLUS
 The northern Vietnamese port city of Hai Phong is wooing more Chinese investors, leveraging its deep-water port, expressways and airport. The city now hosts 823 Chinese-backed projects worth over US$13 billion (RM54 billion).
 2.TECHNOLOGY TO IMPROVE MARINE FORECASTING -- VIETNAMPLUS
 Science, technology, and international cooperation are vital for Vietnam to improve marine forecasting, enable proactive disaster prevention and mitigation, and safeguard coastal communities’ livelihoods.
